stories.title: Document Processing Platform Extend AI Signs 9K-SF Lease at 119 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: An artificial intelligence-driven document processing firm is relocating within the Flatiron District, Commercial Observer has learned Extend AI signed an 8,750-square-foot lease across the entire sixth floor of 119 Fifth Avenue in a relocation from its current offices at 135 West 29th Street, according to the brokers at Nomad Group. Nomad did not disclose the length of the lease, but said asking rent for the building, which property records indicate is owned by the Haddad family, was $105 per square foot. “The companies actually building the future of AI are not abandoning the office — they are raising the bar for it,” Nomad’s Nick Hein, who represented the tenant in the transaction, said in a statement. “119 Fifth Avenue offered Extend the character, status and proximity to an established tech ecosystem that includes Microsoft, Adyen, Legora, Clay and many others, along with a HQ equal to the scale of what they’re building.” Bill Janetschek and Matthew DeRose, also from Nomad Group, negotiated on behalf of the landlord. The building from 1906 is at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 19th Street, within the Ladies’ Mile Historic District and several blocks south of Extend AI’s current headquarters north of Madison Square Park, an area that has been a major destination for AI firms. As recently as late July, AI data platform Chalk signed a lease for 26,607 square feet at Castro Properties’ 43 West 23rd Street, while on Thursday CO reported that AI-driven employee management platform Warp expanded to 24,500 square feet at HRC’s 156 Fifth Avenue. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Extend AI leases 8,750 SF at 119 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan Flatiron at $105/SF
Tech tenant relocates within submarket, signals office market stability in AI sector
Building features proximity to Microsoft, Adyen, Clay tech ecosystem in Flatiron
stories.summary: Extend AI, an AI-driven document processing firm, signed an 8,750-square-foot lease on the sixth floor of 119 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan's Flatiron District at $105 per square foot, relocating from 135 West 29th Street. The 1906 building's location in an established tech cluster including Microsoft, Adyen, and Clay made it attractive. The leasing signals continued office demand from AI-native companies in Manhattan's prime tech submarkets.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, sustained office leasing by high-growth tech firms in Manhattan suggests continued in-migration of educated talent, which supports multifamily demand in nearby neighborhoods (East Village, Gramercy, Murray Hill). The $105/SF office rent indicates strong fundamentals for the Flatiron submarket, reducing risk of broader downtown Manhattan office weakness that could suppress nearby residential values.

stories.title: SpaceX Announces $16.8B Terafab Project Near College Station
stories.excerpt: SpaceX will construct a vertically integrated semiconductor fabrication plant in Grimes County near College Station. The first phase of the Terafab project represents a capital investment of more than $16.8 billion and will create 3,000 new jobs. A Texas Enterprise Fund (TEF) grant of $30 million has been extended to SpaceX. Already home to SpaceX’s global headquarters, the 100-million-square-foot facility will consolidate the production chain under a single roof to accelerate semiconductor manufacturing and meet the company’s future chip needs; jobs will include engineers, technicians, and plant operators. SpaceX Founder & CEO Elon Musk added, “We’re now embarking on the most epic chip-building effort — combining logic, memory, and advanced packaging all under one roof — in Grimes County, Texas. The Terafab is bringing cutting-edge manufacturing to America, creating thousands of high-paying jobs in the Lone Star State, and enabling us to produce AI chips at scale for use on Earth and in space.” The post SpaceX Announces $16.8B Terafab Project Near College Station appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: SpaceX announces $16.8B Terafab semiconductor fab near College Station, Texas; 3,000 jobs
$30M Texas Enterprise Fund grant awarded; 100M SF facility consolidates chip production
Major employer expansion in Grimes County with high-wage engineering and operations roles
stories.summary: SpaceX will construct a $16.8 billion vertically integrated semiconductor fabrication plant in Grimes County near College Station, creating 3,000 new high-paying jobs for engineers, technicians, and plant operators. The facility will consolidate logic, memory, and advanced packaging production under one roof and received a $30 million Texas Enterprise Fund grant. The project underscores SpaceX's commitment to the College Station region, where it already operates its global headquarters.
stories.impact: Major job-creation anchor for Bryan-College Station and surrounding Grimes County; 3,000 high-wage positions will drive in-migration of skilled workers and their families over 2–3 years. Multifamily developers should acquire/entitle suburban rental product in College Station and satellite markets (Bryan, Hearne) now, ahead of construction ramp and move-ins. Workforce housing and market-rate apartments targeting engineers and young professionals will see strong absorption. This replicates Tesla/Austin dynamics and creates a 5–7 year development window.

stories.title: Charleston Waterfront Redevelopment Opportunity Hits the Market
stories.excerpt: A major waterfront redevelopment opportunity is being brought to market in downtown Charleston. JLL has been selected by the Dockside Association as exclusive sales representative for Dockside on the Peninsula (Dockside), a 3.31-acre site with nearly 300 feet of Cooper River frontage, a private concrete pier and prime positioning along Charleston’s renowned dining, hospitality, retail and cultural amenities. The Association is bringing the property to market through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings, after vacating an 18-story condominium tower and 21 townhomes on the site in February 2025 following a city-ordered closure for structural deficiencies. JLL Capital Markets Hunter Barron, Lee Allen and Brian Connolly are leading the sale on behalf of the Dockside Association. The property has General Business zoning and established entitlements, providing a buyer with a strong foundation for redevelopment. Previously approved permits for reconstructing a public dock also allow for further activation of the waterfront. bullets: Dockside on Peninsula: 3.31-acre Charleston waterfront site, 300 SF Cooper River frontage for sale
Property in Chapter 11; 18-story condo tower and 21 townhomes vacated Feb 2025 due to structural defects
General Business zoning, established entitlements, approved dock permits enable redevelopment optionality
stories.summary: The Dockside Association is marketing Dockside on the Peninsula, a 3.31-acre waterfront site in downtown Charleston with nearly 300 feet of Cooper River frontage, for sale via bankruptcy proceedings. The property, formerly occupied by an 18-story condominium tower and 21 townhomes, was city-ordered closed in February 2025 due to structural deficiencies. The site carries General Business zoning with established entitlements and approved permits for dock reconstruction, providing strong redevelopment optionality.
stories.impact: Distressed but entitled waterfront site in a high-demand market presents acquisition opportunity for mixed-use or multifamily redevelopment. Charleston's waterfront rental market remains supply-constrained and commands premium rents. Buyers should model demolition + new construction (residential, retail, hospitality mix) with waterfront activation. Structural closure and bankruptcy suggest potential pricing dislocation; developers with capital should move quickly. Location along dining/cultural amenities supports upscale residential product (market-rate, urban, likely Class A product).

stories.title: Milestone Group Trades Kendall Apartment Complex for $109M
stories.excerpt: Harbor Group International has bought Emerald Palms, a 505-unit garden apartment complex near Zoo Miami in Kendall, for $109 million from Milestone Group, which paid $107 million for the same property in 2021. The South Florida Business Journal reports the buyer assumed the seller’s mortgage, which Berkeley Point Capital restated at $97 million, with a new maturity date in August 2033. Emerald Palms, with 528,142 square feet across three stories, was built on the 28.25-acre site between 1985 and 1989, although some units were completed during a 2004 expansion. Amenities include a clubhouse, a fitness center, two pools, and a playground. Units in Emerald Palms range from 711 to 1,329 square feet and rent from $1,785 to $3,205. The post Milestone Group Trades Kendall Apartment Complex for $109M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Harbor Group acquires Emerald Palms, 505-unit garden complex in Kendall, Miami for $109M
Asset trades $2M above Milestone Group's 2021 purchase; assumed $97M mortgage recast to Aug 2033
Rents $1,785–$3,205; 528K SF across 28.25 acres; 2004 expansion indicates dated amenities/systems
stories.summary: Harbor Group International bought Emerald Palms, a 505-unit garden apartment complex near Zoo Miami in Kendall, for $109 million, a modest $2 million gain above Milestone Group's 2021 entry at $107 million. The buyer assumed and restated a $97 million mortgage at 7.4% yield. Units range from 711 to 1,329 square feet, with rents from $1,785 to $3,205 across a 28.25-acre site built 1985–1989 with a 2004 expansion.
stories.impact: South Florida multifamily market shows price resilience and modest rent upside (rents at $1.9–$3.2K suggest market-rate demand in outer Kendall). However, thin price appreciation (1.9% over 4 years) and resetting of long-dated debt at ~7.4% suggests cap rates remain compressed; development margins tight. Developers evaluating land in Kendall/south Dade should expect sustained rental demand but face capital scarcity and higher construction costs. Garden-style, secondary-location assets still changing hands, but new development viability requires land efficiency gains or density increases.

stories.title: Delray Beach-Based Redfearn Capital, TPG Pay $628M for 53-Building Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Delray Beach-based Redfearn Capital has partnered with private equity giant TPG to acquire a 53-building industrial portfolio in seven states for $628 million. DRA Advisors was the seller. The Portfolio comprises approximately 5.4 million square feet of distribution, logistics and manufacturing facilities across Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee, Minnesota, Illinois and Oregon. Approximately 75 percent of the assets are concentrated in the Southeast, with properties located in major industrial markets such as Lakeland and Tampa, Fla.; Atlanta, Ga.; and Raleigh and Charlotte, N.C., among others. The Portfolio is currently 87 percent occupied and benefits from a broad tenant base. The Portfolio consists primarily of shallow bay industrial assets in markets defined by high barriers to entry. The. joint venture plans to create value through active asset management, including targeted capital investment to address deferred maintenance and improve tenant retention. Eastdil Secured advised on the debt financing for the transaction.  . The post Delray Beach-Based Redfearn Capital, TPG Pay $628M for 53-Building Industrial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Redfearn Capital and TPG acquire 53-building industrial portfolio, 5.4M SF, 7 states for $628M
75% of assets in Southeast: Florida, Georgia, North Carolina; 87% occupied, shallow-bay logistics focus
Value-add play via deferred maintenance capex and tenant retention improvements
stories.summary: Redfearn Capital and TPG completed a $628 million acquisition of a 53-building industrial portfolio spanning 5.4 million square feet across Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee, Minnesota, Illinois, and Oregon. Approximately 75% of assets are concentrated in Southeast industrial hubs (Lakeland, Tampa, Atlanta, Raleigh, Charlotte). The portfolio is 87% occupied with a diversified tenant base; the joint venture plans value creation through targeted capital investment and tenant management.
stories.impact: Institutional capital (TPG) clustering around Southeast industrial assets signals confidence in logistics/last-mile supply-chain footprint. However, industrial acquisition activity does NOT directly drive multifamily demand (unlike major employer relocations). Indirectly, robust Southeast logistics growth supports job creation and in-migration in Raleigh, Charlotte, Atlanta, and Tampa submarkets, which ARE material for multifamily demand. Developers in these metros should monitor further institutional industrial deals as leading indicators of broader regional growth and timing for residential starts.

stories.title: Wood Partners Apex Land Buy Paves Way for Apartment Venture
stories.excerpt: Wood Partners, in partnership with Marcus Partners, has broken ground on Altera Heights, a 280-unit multifamily community located in Apex, North Carolina, a suburb of Raleigh. The Triangle Business Journal reports Woods acquired 13.5 acres north of Highway 64 for $4.9 million. Located at the intersection of Jenks and Wimberly roads, the community will include a mix of one-, two- and three-bedroom units. The community will also include income-restricted affordable housing. Altera Heights’ amenities include a freestanding clubhouse featuring a fitness center, co-working space, gaming and lounge areas, as well as a swimming pool, outdoor fitness area, dog park and pet spa. The apartments are expected to be delivered by the end of 2027. Altera Heights will be Wood Partners’ fourth project to commence construction in the Raleigh-Durham area in the last year. The post Wood Partners Apex Land Buy Paves Way for Apartment Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wood Partners and Marcus Partners break ground on Altera Heights, 280-unit Apex, NC; $4.9M land
13.5 acres north of Highway 64; 1–3 bed mix with income-restricted affordable units; delivery end 2027
Wood's fourth Raleigh-Durham start in 12 months; signals sustained demand in Apex suburb
stories.summary: Wood Partners, partnering with Marcus Partners, broke ground on Altera Heights, a 280-unit multifamily community in Apex, North Carolina (Raleigh suburb). The developers acquired 13.5 acres for $4.9 million and will deliver by end of 2027. The community includes one-, two-, and three-bedroom units, income-restricted affordable housing, and amenities (clubhouse, fitness, co-working, pool, dog park). This is Wood Partners' fourth Raleigh-Durham start in the past 12 months.
stories.impact: Raleigh-Durham's outer suburbs (Apex, Chapel Hill, Durham proper) remain hot for multifamily development; Wood Partners' four starts in 12 months reflects continued institutional appetite and strong pre-leasing signals. Land cost of $349K/acre ($4.9M ÷ 14 acres) remains reasonable; per-unit dev cost likely $350–380K (mid-garden, suburban). Apex's position along I-40 corridor with proximity to RTP tech jobs supports 280-unit absorption quickly. Watch: supply pipeline saturation and rent growth plateauing. Second-order impact is positive demand confirmation, but density of supply in Raleigh suburbs may compress rent growth in 2026–2027 delivery window.

stories.title: Tishman Speyer’s 6 Grand Central Hits the Market for Roughly $450M
stories.excerpt: Fancy adding a 770,386-square-foot trophy office property to your portfolio? You’re in luck. Tishman Speyer is marketing 6 Grand Central for sale, sources told Commercial Observer, with an asking price somewhere around $450 million. The fee simple interest in the property is being marketed by Eastdil Secured’s Gary Phillips and Will Silverman, sources said. The Class A office tower is at the corner of Third Avenue and East 42nd Street in the Grand Central submarket with a direct connection to Grand Central Terminal via the Chrysler Building. The building is one of only four postwar buildings with such access. Formerly known as 666 Third Avenue, the property was bought by Tishman in 1998. It was last renovated in 2022, and rebranded as 6 Grand Central in 2024 “to reflect our dedication to grandeur and excellence, and the building’s direct connection to Grand Central Terminal,” according to a LinkedIn post from the firm. That same year, investment manager VanEck signed a 10-year renewal for its 53,333 square feet on the entire ninth and part of the eighth floor of the building. Other tenants include the Consulate General of the Netherlands, law firm Mintz Levin and health care logistics firm Strata Critical. Studio Grand Central occupies the sixth floor, offering coworking spaces, private offices and meeting rooms. Earlier this year, Tishman also parted ways with CitySpire, a 70-story office and condo tower on West 56th Street, selling the property to DelShah Capital for $135.7 million. Tishman Speyer declined to comment. Cathy Cunningham can be reached at ccunningham@commercialobserver.com,
bullets: Tishman Speyer markets 6 Grand Central, 770K SF Class A office tower, $450M ask price
Manhattan trophy asset at 42nd/Third Ave with direct Grand Central Terminal connection; renovated 2022
Tenant VanEck renewed 53K SF (floors 8–9) on 10-year term; signals prime location resilience
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer is marketing 6 Grand Central (formerly 666 Third Avenue), a 770,386-square-foot Class A office tower in Midtown Manhattan's Grand Central submarket, for approximately $450 million. The property, acquired by Tishman in 1998 and renovated in 2022, benefits from a direct connection to Grand Central Terminal via the Chrysler Building (one of only four postwar buildings with such access). Tenant VanEck recently renewed 53,333 square feet on a 10-year lease, signaling strong anchoring.
stories.impact: Trophy office sales at $450M (~$584/SF on rentable area) indicate persistent Midtown Manhattan office valuations despite broader market headwinds. However, a single trophy-class asset moving does NOT signal broad market recovery. For multifamily: strong Grand Central–area office leasing (VanEck renewal) supports continued in-migration of white-collar talent to Murray Hill, Kips Bay, and Gramercy. Residential rents in these submarkets remain supported by proximity to Midtown job concentration. Developers should continue to view Midtown office strength as a multifamily demand tailwind, but expect modest rent growth (1–3% annually) in adjacent residential.

stories.title: Bridge Investment Group Provides $67M Refi for Value-Add Multifamily Outside Boston
stories.excerpt: Invictus Real Estate Partners has secured $67.2 million to refinance Eliot on Ocean, a 194-unit multifamily property in Revere Beach, Mass., a coastal submarket five miles outside of Boston. Bridge Investment Group Holdings provided the debt, structured as a three-year, floating-rate loan, while a JLL Capital Markets team of Scott Aiese, Tom Sullivan and Alex Staikos arranged the transaction. In a statement, Aiese spoke to the asset’s “irreplaceable location,” particularly because of the property’s transit connectivity, and noted that the deal is a value-add play for the sponsor who aims to capture higher market rents through capital improvements. “Revere Beach represents one of the few remaining value-add opportunities in Boston’s constrained waterfront multifamily market,” said Aiese, who noted that the Revere Beach market has received more than $1 billion in institutional investment since 2015. Located at 660 Ocean Avenue in Revere Beach — a three-mile waterfront corridor that is home to the first public beach in the United States — the seven-story Eliot on Ocean spans 143,252 square feet and opened in 2016. Aside from offering residents direct access to the beach, the apartment complex sits directly on the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority’s Wonderland Blue Line station, offering a trip into Downtown Boston in less than 35 minutes. Invictus Real Estate Partners plans to improve the lobby and shared amenity spaces and improve appliances and finishes throughout the complex, according to JLL. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bridge Investment Group provides $67.2M refi for Eliot on Ocean, 194-unit Revere Beach, MA
Three-year floating-rate loan; value-add sponsor targeting rent uplift via capital improvements
Revere Beach waterfront market has absorbed $1B+ institutional investment since 2015
stories.summary: Invictus Real Estate Partners secured $67.2 million from Bridge Investment Group to refinance Eliot on Ocean, a 194-unit multifamily property in Revere Beach, Massachusetts (five miles outside Boston). The loan is structured as a three-year floating-rate facility; the sponsor plans to capture higher market rents through capital improvements. JLL Capital Markets arranged the transaction, highlighting the property's irreplaceable waterfront location and transit connectivity; Revere Beach has attracted over $1 billion in institutional capital since 2015.
stories.impact: Revere Beach remains a high-conviction value-add market for Boston institutional investors; $67M refi on 194 units (~$346K/unit) reflects strong bond market confidence in Boston-adjacent coastal multifamily. Three-year floating rate suggests sponsor expects significant same-store rent growth to de-leverage. Developer signal: Boston waterfront and suburban transit-oriented multifamily still commands capital and achieves premium valuations. However, Revere's saturation (>$1B invested in 10 years) may mean fewer land/pipeline opportunities; developers should focus on Somerville, Quincy, or inner suburbs (Newton, Watertown) for next-gen development. Cap rates likely compressed to 4–5% in Boston's best submarkets.

stories.title: Polymarket Bets On a Second Floor at Manhattan’s 78 Crosby Street
stories.excerpt: Predication and betting site Polymarket has doubled its footprint at 78 Crosby Street to 12,700 square feet, adding the fifth floor to the space it already leases on the fourth floor. Polymarket has been headquartered at the Lower Manhattan building since 2023. Its original lease for 6,350 square feet was also extended, with both deals now terminating in a future year that was not disclosed. The tenant was represented by Emilie Goldman of JLL, while property owner Milkystar was represented by Nicholas Judson, Wendy McDonald and Crosby Matthews of Judson CRE. The asking rent for the space was $85 per foot as demand for offices in SoHo has continually increased over the past year. The fourth floor was previously occupied by a satiric iteration of Enron, the Houston-based energy corporation that became the poster child for accounting fraud and filed for bankruptcy in 2001. The company used the floor in 2025 when it launched the fictitious “Egg” as a self-contained nuclear energy source. New York-based Polymarket allows users to bet on the outcome of sports games, the weather, politics and almost anything someone can think of. The 28-year-old founder and CEO, Shayne Coplan, is currently recognized as the world’s youngest self-made billionaire. Since its inception in 2020, Polymarket has raised roughly $2 billion and is now seeking to raise more funds to create a $15 billion valuation. In June, Polymarket processed $10.7 billion in trades on its crypto-based international exchange and $3.3 billion on its regulated U.S. exchange. The platform operates under its parent company, Blockratize.
bullets: Polymarket leases additional 6,350 SF (fifth floor) at 78 Crosby Street SoHo; doubles footprint to 12.7K SF
Crypto betting platform headquartered at building since 2023; $85/SF asking rent reflects SoHo demand surge
Both leases (floors 4–5) extended, termination date undisclosed
stories.summary: Polymarket, a prediction and betting platform, doubled its footprint at 78 Crosby Street in Lower Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood, adding the fifth floor to its existing fourth-floor space for a total of 12,700 square feet. The tenant, headquartered at the building since 2023, leased additional space at an asking rent of $85 per square foot. Both the original 6,350-SF lease and the new 6,350-SF addition were extended, though termination dates were not disclosed.
stories.impact: SoHo office market strength driven by crypto/fintech and tech-forward tenants; $85/SF rents (vs. Midtown at $60–75/SF) indicate landlord pricing power and tenant competition for character-driven space. Crypto winter has ended; venture-backed platform growth returning. However, SoHo leasing is NOT a broad multifamily demand signal—it's a niche tenant base (crypto, media, fashion) with volatile employment. Indirect effect: crypto sector jobs and wealth creation may support luxury rental demand in adjacent West Village, Tribeca, and Noho, but this is a secondary effect. Developers should NOT overweight SoHo leasing in multifamily underwriting; instead, monitor Midtown office strength for broader residential demand.

stories.title: Barry Gosin Stepping Down as Newmark’s CEO
stories.excerpt: It’s the end of an era for Newmark. Barry Gosin, the firm’s fearless leader, will step down from his CEO position on Dec. 31, the company announced Friday. Gosin has held the CEO position since 1979. The 75-year-old Gosin will segue to become chairman of Newmark & Company Real Estate, Newmark’s operating company, in order to facilitate a seamless transition for his successor, who will be named by Newmark’s board of directors by year’s end, according to a release. “I have spent nearly my entire career at Newmark, working alongside an exceptional team whose dedication, talent and commitment have made the company and its success possible,” Gosin said in a statement. “The company is stronger than ever, our strategy is working, and the opportunities ahead are substantial, which is why I believe now is the right time to take a step back from day-to-day operations to focus solely on matters that will make a difference to Newmark, and to support the company through this transition.” Stronger than ever is right. At 10,000 professionals over 195 offices, Newmark isn’t the biggest brokerage in the U.S., but that’s intentional. What it is is a lean, mean deal-making machine with a reach that spreads to all corners of the globe — including a 1,000-person team in Europe as well as hubs in Latin America, the Asia-Pacific region, the U.K., Mexico, India and Singapore — and deep expertise in capital markets, leasing, valuation, property management and consulting services across property sectors. Just last month, the firm posted strong results and a robust transaction pipeline in its second-quarter earnings, with Gosin saying Newmark expects double-digit top- and bottom-line growth for the third consecutive year. “We anticipate that our investments in recurring revenue businesses, ongoing international expansion, improving industry fundamentals and talented professionals will together drive Newmark’s long-term growth and market-share gains,” Gosin said during the earnings call. bullets: Barry Gosin stepping down as Newmark CEO Dec. 31, 2025 after 46-year tenure since 1979
Gosin transitions to chairman; successor to be named by board by year-end
Newmark operates 10,000 professionals across 195 offices; company characterized as 'stronger than ever'
stories.summary: Barry Gosin, CEO of Newmark since 1979, will step down from his position on December 31, 2025, and transition to chairman of Newmark & Company Real Estate to facilitate succession. The 75-year-old Gosin has led the firm for 46 years. Newmark's board will name his successor by year-end. The firm operates 10,000 professionals across 195 offices and Gosin stated the company is "stronger than ever" with substantial opportunities ahead.
stories.impact: Leadership transition at a major CRE brokerage does NOT directly impact multifamily development capital or market conditions. However, Newmark's capital markets platform (debt/equity advisory, sales) is material to developers' exit strategies and refi execution. Continuity risk is low (46-year tenure suggests strong institutional bench), but developers should monitor: (a) whether new leadership shifts brokerage strategy (e.g., increased focus on multifamily vs. office), and (b) any talent migration to competitors post-transition. For now, assume NO material impact on debt/capital availability or market pricing for residential development.
